clue.text: Fashionable ring snatched by father as a publicity stunt

indicators.note: what is snatched is held in the grasp of the snatcher, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: pop is an informal word for a dad
something hot is in vogue
the letter O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A dad grabs a trendy ring from someone purely to get attention in the press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snatched by' makes the father the container: the other two pieces sit inside him, splitting him around the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A photo opportunity is an event staged so cameras can record a politician or celebrity, which is exactly a publicity stunt.

clue.text: Die from excitement if information is missing

indicators.note: whatever is missing has been left out, so a letter must be removed from the word

parts.note: passion is strong excitement or emotion
I is the standard abbreviation for information, as on tourist signs

explanation.surface: Someone dies of over-excitement when they are kept in the dark.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the I out of PASSION and PASS ON remains. 'Die from excitement' reads as one phrase, but 'Die' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass on is a gentle euphemism for dying, used to soften talk of death.

clue.text: Some clergy attack centres enforcing vow of silence …

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle, so only the innermost letters of each word are kept

parts.note: the two middle letters of this four-letter word
the two middle letters of this six-letter word
the two middle letters of this six-letter word

explanation.surface: Monks or priests force a strict silence on their order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some clergy' looks like a selection from one word, but 'Some' is itself one of the three words whose middles are taken.
explanation.definitionFit: Omertà is the Mafia's code of silence, a sworn refusal to talk to the police about crimes.

clue.text: … disgraced monk's status, perhaps, for not following the rules

definitions.meaning: first meaning: expelled from a religious order

explanation.surface: Continuing from the previous clue, a monk is thrown out for breaking his vows.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is a literal reading of the phrase, an order being a community of monks; 'perhaps' warns that it is one example.
explanation.definitionFit: In a meeting or in conduct, out of order means breaching the agreed procedure or acceptable behaviour.

clue.text: Gone on central Iraqi food

parts.note: what has gone is past

indicators.note: central means at the very middle, so only the middle letter of the word is used

parts.note: the middle letter of this five-letter word

explanation.surface: Someone is hooked on the food of central Iraq.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gone on' looks like 'keen on', but 'Gone' is PAST and 'on' simply puts it before the next piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasta, such as spaghetti or penne, is a staple Italian food made from wheat dough.

clue.text: Attack head demonstrating evolutionary survival principle

parts.note: a sudden attack of coughing or rage is a fit
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Dungeness

explanation.surface: A scientist confronts the central idea of Darwin's theory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' here is a promontory of land, not a person's head or a leader; NESS appears in many British place names for headlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Survival of the fittest is Darwin's principle, and fitness is the biological measure of how well an organism survives and reproduces.

clue.text: Non-national enemy seizes power with queen

indicators.note: to seize something is to grip it, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: a foe is an enemy
a reign is a period of sovereign power
R stands for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: An enemy from abroad stages a coup and grabs the throne alongside the queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen' tempts ER, but only a single R is needed at the end; R for Regina appears on royal cyphers.
explanation.definitionFit: A foreigner is someone who is not a citizen of the country in question, hence a non-national.

clue.text: Girl embodying Margaret Thatcher's single-minded approach

definitions.meaning: second meaning: an acronym of her slogan 'There is no alternative'

explanation.surface: A young woman personifies the Iron Lady's uncompromising attitude.
explanation.walkthrough: Margaret Thatcher was the British prime minister of the 1980s, whose insistence that there was no alternative to her economic policy was shortened to an acronym.
explanation.definitionFit: The initials of 'There is no alternative' spell a common woman's name, summing up an unbending political stance.

clue.text: Greet men excited to be coming out

indicators.note: excited things are agitated and stirred up, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Fans welcome people stepping out of a building, thrilled to see them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Excited' reads as describing the men, but it tells you to rearrange the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Emergent describes something in the process of appearing or arising, so it is in the act of coming out.

clue.text: Sell important means to create capital

parts.note: to shift goods is informal for selling them
a key issue is an important one

explanation.surface: A businessman explains that selling is the vital way to raise funds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' suggests money, but here it is a capital letter on a keyboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Holding down this keyboard button turns a typed lowercase letter into an uppercase one.

clue.text: Work hard with women in constituency

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a parliamentary constituency is a seat
W is the abbreviation for women, as on toilet doors

explanation.surface: An MP toils away with the female voters of their district.
explanation.walkthrough: In British politics a seat is an electoral district held by a member of parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: To sweat over a task is to labour strenuously at it, as if perspiring with effort.

clue.text: Develop green site as a place for animal sanctuary

indicators.note: to develop land is to rework and rebuild it, so the letters are remodelled into a new form

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A planning proposal to turn a patch of greenfield land into a wildlife refuge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Develop' sounds like property planning, which fits the surface, but it is a signal to rearrange the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Serengeti is a vast Tanzanian national park famous for protecting wildebeest, lions and other wildlife.

clue.text: Stripped almost without thinking

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a monk or nun taken out of their robe
second meaning: done automatically, by routine

explanation.walkthrough: A habit is the robe worn by a monk or nun, so being out of it means undressed; this echoes the monks of earlier clues.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something by routine means acting automatically, with little conscious thought, through repetition.

clue.text: Clean out natural gas producer!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: remove the insides, as of a fish
second meaning: the digestive tract, which makes wind

explanation.walkthrough: 'Natural gas' suggests the fossil fuel, but the joke is the body's own wind from the intestines.
explanation.definitionFit: Gutting a fish or building removes its interior; the intestines generate flatulence as they digest food.

clue.text: Reprimands dashed racer's hope

indicators.note: something dashed is smashed to pieces, so the letters are broken up and reassembled

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A driver is scolded and his ambitions of winning are ruined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dashed hopes' is a stock phrase, so 'dashed' seems to belong with 'hope', yet it governs the letters of both following words.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are verbs meaning to scold or express disapproval of someone's conduct.

clue.text: Nice earner I'd abandoned to become comedy act

indicators.note: abandoned can mean wild and uninhibited, so the letters are let loose into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Someone gives up a well-paid job to try a career in stand-up.
explanation.walkthrough: Eric Morecambe and Ernie Wise were a hugely popular British TV double act from the 1960s to the 1980s.
explanation.definitionFit: The pair performed together on stage and television as one of Britain's best-loved comic partnerships.

clue.text: Proper support for journalist's text can stop others using it

definitions.note: a clause describing the thing; the answer is a noun

indicators.note: in a down clue a support sits underneath, so this piece comes after the other

parts.note: copy is the text a journalist files
right means correct or proper

explanation.surface: A reporter's article, properly protected, can prevent others from lifting it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description rather than a synonym: the answer is the thing that can stop others using the text.
explanation.definitionFit: Copyright is the legal right of an author to control reproduction, which lets them prevent unauthorised use of their work.

clue.text: Ship requires check-in before this

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: sooner than now means earlier, before this moment
CH is chess notation for check

explanation.surface: Boarding a vessel means checking in first, just like at an airport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Check-in' reads as one hyphenated noun, but it splits into a piece and its placement instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A schooner is a sailing vessel with two or more masts and fore-and-aft rigged sails.

clue.text: Being ignorant, I abandoned everything on date

definitions.note: a participle phrase; the answer is an adjective

indicators.note: what is abandoned is left behind, so a letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: the universe is everything there is
taken as written
D is the abbreviation for date

explanation.surface: Someone confesses they gave up all their plans for a romantic evening out of naivety.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the I from UNIVERSE and add D for date.
explanation.definitionFit: To be unversed in a subject is to lack knowledge or experience of it, hence uninformed.

clue.text: Absurd poem in difficult setting — so modern

indicators.note: a setting holds a jewel in place, so one piece is mounted inside another

parts.note: a contrary person is awkward and difficult

indicators.note: something absurd is nonsensical, so the letters are jumbled into a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A critic finds a nonsense poem with an obscure setting very up to date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In difficult setting' reads as describing the poem's backdrop, but it places the jumbled poem inside the word for difficult.
explanation.definitionFit: Contemporary describes things belonging to the present day, the same sense as current or up to date.

clue.text: That salamander of mine sounds so small

indicators.note: what something sounds like is what the ear hears, so the spoken form counts here

parts.note: a newt is a small salamander, and it belongs to me

explanation.surface: A proud pet owner points out how tiny their amphibian is.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is pronounced my-NEWT when it means tiny, not like the unit of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Pronounced with stress on the second syllable, the word is an adjective for something extremely tiny.

clue.text: Standard part of working is negotiating to get promoted

indicators.note: promotion means going up, and in a down clue going up means reading from bottom to top
a part of a phrase is a portion of it, so the letters are found inside the words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, the second word and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Normally, a part of doing a job well is bargaining your way up the ladder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Promoted' has a career sense that suits the surface, but in a down clue it means read upwards. An ensign is also a junior naval officer, a neat echo of promotion.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a flag carried as an emblem, and an ensign is a flag flown by a ship to show nationality.

clue.text: Formal person you can become in posh company?

definitions.text: Formal person you can become in posh company?

parts.words: Formal person you can become in posh company?
parts.note: surface reading: a stiff, formal individual you might turn into among the upper classes; setter's reading: the pronoun that genteel speakers use in place of an informal 'you'

explanation.walkthrough: 'Person' is grammatical: the word is a formal pronoun, and in upper-class speech 'you' becomes it, as in 'one does one's best'.
explanation.definitionFit: This impersonal pronoun replaces the generic 'you' in formal or upper-class English speech.

clue.text: Watering can create inconvenience, when getting time in for golf

indicators.note: putting one thing in for another means swapping it into its place, so one letter replaces another

parts.note: irritation is annoyance caused by an inconvenience
T is the abbreviation for time
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Sprinklers on a course can annoy golfers when they have booked a tee time.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay runs backwards: the answer becomes IRRITATION when T goes in place of G, so to solve, swap the T of IRRITATION for G.
explanation.definitionFit: Irrigation is supplying water to land or crops through channels, pipes or sprinklers.

clue.text: Patriarch begins investigating some American alternative cults

indicators.note: what begins something comes at its start, so only the opening letter of each word is used

parts.note: the opening letters of the five words

explanation.surface: A family head starts looking into fringe religious groups in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Patriarch begins' looks like the start of the patriarch's story, but 'begins' points at the following five words.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Isaac, son of Abraham and father of Jacob, is one of the three biblical patriarchs of Israel.

clue.text: Suffer stomach nick

definitions.meaning: third meaning: steal, nick being British slang for stealing

explanation.surface: Someone endures a cut to the belly.
explanation.walkthrough: Three separate meanings: 'stomach' and 'nick' look like nouns, a belly and a cut, but both are verbs; nick is British slang for steal.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers enduring a blow, tolerating something unpleasant and stealing property.

clue.text: Lost again in reverie about the past …

indicators.note: something lost is astray and disoriented, so the letters wander into a new order

parts.note: taken as written: the indicator word is also part of the letters

explanation.surface: Someone drifts away once more, daydreaming about bygone days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lost' does double duty, signalling the rearrangement while supplying its own letters to the mix with 'again'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nostalgia is a sentimental longing for an earlier period, a wistful daydream of times gone by.

clue.text: … time I linked with a beautiful young woman

parts.note: an hour is a period of time
taken as written

explanation.surface: Continuing the daydream, the dreamer recalls a time spent with a lovely young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: A houri is a word rarely met outside crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: In Islamic tradition a houri is a beautiful maiden of paradise, and the word came to mean any alluring young woman.

clue.text: Paltry sum socialist said was mailed

parts.note: red is a common label for a left-winger

indicators.note: what is said is spoken, so a word is judged by its pronunciation here

parts.note: a mailed letter was sent

explanation.surface: A left-winger mentions that only a tiny amount was posted to them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Said' sits after 'socialist' so seems to report speech, but it applies only to the mailing.
explanation.definitionFit: Not a red cent is an American idiom for no money at all, the copper cent being the smallest coin.

clue.text: Research facility in Switzerland retains first reservoir

indicators.note: to retain something is to keep hold of it, so one piece is kept inside another

parts.note: CERN is the particle physics laboratory near Geneva
1st, read as the letters IST

explanation.surface: A Swiss laboratory holds on to its original water store.
explanation.walkthrough: The numeral 1 doubles as the letter I, so the abbreviation 1st becomes IST.
explanation.definitionFit: A cistern is a tank for storing water, a small-scale reservoir.
